title: Mulberry Analytics Hosted Embeddings + Rerank API Walkthrough
summary: Redwood AE+SE demoed hosted embeddings + reranking endpoints for Mulberry Analytics' product search. Covered retrieval architecture, candidate generation vs. cross-encoder rerank, latency/cost tradeoffs, security questions (SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS) and next steps for pilot and benchmark run in their staging environment.
action_items: Jordan Kim: Send tailored pricing estimate and two pilot options (hosted basic + dedicated trial) - due 2027-12-10
Priya Nair: Share rerank sample prompts and candidate/labeling template - due 2027-12-09
Tom Alvarez: Provide sample index metadata schema and a subset of anonymized queries for benchmark - due 2027-12-13
next_steps: Redwood to run a 2-day hosted benchmark on Mulberry's sample queries (Jordan & Priya)
Customer to provision staging API key and share SSO admin contact for docs access
Schedule technical deep dive on architecture with Platform team next week (Tom + Priya + SE)

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-12-07 | Start: 16:00 UTC | Duration: 52m
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Aisha (Mulberry Head of Search), Tom (Platform), Lina (Data)

Summary (auto): Quick hosted API walkthrough focused on embeddings + rerank. Discussed retrieval/re-rank split, cost/latency tradeoffs and security concerns.

--- Topics: hosted embeddings endpoint, rerank cross-encoder, batching and caching, privacy/KMS, pilot/benchmarks

--- Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. um I'll do a 2 minute intro then Priya will walk through the live demo.
[00:12] Aisha: Thanks Jordan, excited to see how Redwood's hosted endpoints can help our search quality. We're mostly on a Faiss-based candidate store today.
[00:21] Priya: Cool. so quick agenda, embeddings ingestion, candidate retrieval, then the rerank endpoint which is a cross-encoder style model, and finally how to tune latency vs cost.
[00:35] Tom: Quick context, our latency target is 180ms p95 for search, and we run around 120 qps with batched traffic during peak. Cost is also a big factor — we want to avoid multiplier increases when we add rerank.
[00:48] Priya: yeah, that makes sense. two common patterns: 1) retrieve top-k from vector DB then run a cheap bi-encoder rerank, or 2) run a cross-encoder rerank on top-20 candidates for best quality but higher cost/latency. Redwood's hosted API supports both flows and you can pick model variants.
[01:10] Lina: When you say model variants, do you mean different quantized sizes? We care about memory and throughput.
[01:16] Priya: Exactly. we have quantized variants that reduce GPU memory and increase throughput with a small quality delta. We also auto-suggest batching sizes based on sequence length distribution via Optimize recommendations in the Console.
[01:28] Aisha: Is that the same Optimize thing in the console we saw in the quickstart? I thought Optimize also suggests cache policies.
[01:33] Jordan: Yup, Optimize is the cost/perf toolkit. it will recommend batch sizes, prefix/K V cache heuristics and suggest a rerank depth for your SLO. small note — sometimes the Console screenshot generator writes K V cache as "K V cache" in docs, so ignore that little formatting quirk.
[01:48] Tom: For our stack, we use FAISS and Milvus in different products. Any opinion on retrieval? Pinecone is a service we used in the past but we'd like fewer moving parts.
[01:58] Priya: No hard opinion. Redwood's hosted embeddings API returns normalized vectors; you can push them to any vector DB. For the live demo I'll show retrieval simulated in memory then call the rerank endpoint hosted in Redwood to compute cross-encoder scores.
[02:15] Priya: (screen share) Ok here's the API flow: /v1/embeddings -> store vectors -> /v1/retrieval query -> top-k -> /v1/rerank pass candidates + query -> get final ranking. We demoed a small example with product search where the rerank switched the top-1 to a more relevant SKU.
[02:40] Aisha: Nice. How do you handle prefix caching or KV cache? We have a lot of short queries for product facets.
[02:45] Priya: Redwood supports prefix caching for repeated prefixes and a KV cache for decoder-style outputs — less relevant to rerank flows but Optimize will flag high reuse patterns. For embeddings + rerank, we usually rely on candidate caching and result-level caching.
[02:58] Lina: Are there endpoints for batch reranking? We might want to do offline re-ranking during indexing.
[03:03] Priya: Yeah there's a batch rerank path — you can submit a batch job to rerank N queries against a set of candidates. It's asynchronous and good for offline label generation.
[03:13] Tom: Can you talk about end-to-end latency if we do cross-encoder rerank on top-20? Ballpark numbers with hosted?
[03:19] Priya: For a mid-sized cross-encoder model on hosted, expect ~60-180ms per request for rerank depending on sequence length and batch. If you do top-20 with a compact quantized model you can be under 120ms but YMMV. The recomposed flow will add retrieval time — so overall on our side people often hit 150-250ms.
[03:41] Aisha: That's within our p95 target if tuned. How about cost then? Does Redwood provide cost-per-call estimates?
[03:47] Jordan: Yes, the Console gives token-level and model-level cost breakdowns. we can also provide an estimated cost-per-query for a given top-k and model combo during pilot.
[03:56] Lina: Security: we handle PII, so data residency and KMS are must-haves. Is hosted allowed?
[04:03] Jordan: For customers with strict PII needs we offer Private deployments, but hosted can be used with strict TOS: we support customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest and SOC2 Type II compliance. We'll share the SOC2 report and KMS integration guide.
[04:17] Tom: Any log retention options? We need short retention in staging and longer for production audits.
[04:22] Priya: You can configure log retention per-project in Console; audit logs can be exported and we also integrate with SIEMs.
[04:29] Aisha: Curious about model switching and fallbacks if capacity spikes. We don't want user-visible errors.
[04:36] Priya: Redwood's routing supports fallback model variants and region failover. for hosted, you can configure automatic fallback to a cheaper or smaller model if latency SLOs are threatened.
[04:46] Jordan: quick note — sometimes the auto-transcription in our recording service will render product names oddly, e.g., "Redwood Optimize" becomes "Redwood optymize" in the transcript, but the Console UI is consistent.
[04:59] Priya: Demo: here's a sample curl to embeddings endpoint (we pasted a short snippet). Then we showed sending candidates into rerank endpoint with payload: {query, candidates: [{id, text, metadata}...]} and got back scores.
[05:20] Lina: We saw earlier that you allow returning structured outputs; can rerank output structured explanations?
[05:25] Priya: Yes, the rerank endpoint can optionally return explanation tokens and a short rationale string. keep in mind explanations cost more in compute but helpful for auditing labels.
[05:37] Tom: For the pilot, we want to run Redwood's hosted rerank against our staging subset with 10k queries. Can you run that for us?
[05:43] Jordan: Absolutely. We'll run a 48-hour benchmark and return metrics: p50/p95 latency, throughput, and cost. Priya will own the run.
[05:50] Aisha: Great. On labeling, we do pairwise judgments. Do you have tooling to ingest pairwise labels into rerank training?
[05:57] Priya: We have export/import formats for pairwise and NDCG-style labels. We'll share templates.
[06:05] Jordan: question from the chat — competitor comparisons? We fielded a few questions versus OpenAI's embeddings and Anthropic; Redwood focuses on production serving and predictable economics.
[06:18] Lina: A couple of small clarifications: 1) can the rerank call be proxied through our edge? 2) do you support SAML SSO for the Console?
[06:25] Priya: 1) yes you can proxy requests via your edge, just watch for additional latency; 2) yes SAML/SSO is supported and we can add SSO admins to your tenant.
[06:36] (longer demo silence while SE runs a live example)
[08:12] Priya: ok here's a more interesting example — query: "waterproof hiking boots for wide feet"; initial top-10 had mismatches, the cross-encoder rerank promoted the better SKU because it matched attribute "wide" and materials, showing rerank helps with compositional queries.
[08:39] Aisha: that's the kind of uplift we need. Any idea how to measure quality before/after?
[08:45] Priya: We recommend A/B testing with a labeled holdout and track CTR, add-to-cart and manual relevance scores. Optimize can also run evaluation tests against prompt sets and track regressions.
[09:01] Tom: about data passing: does Redwood persist queries and candidates long term? we want short retention for staging and encrypted storage in prod.
[09:08] Jordan: retention is configurable; we can set short TTLs for dev; for prod you can also enable audit export and KMS-backed storage.
[09:16] Aisha: Ok good. Let's talk timeline: we want a pilot within the next two weeks and a production decision in Q1.
[09:23] Jordan: Sounds reasonable. We'll send the pilot options and schedule the bench.
[09:28] (minor crosstalk)
[09:35] Priya: quick technical note — when you do top-k retrieval, candidate metadata helps rerank massively (brand, category, specs). pass that metadata in the candidate objects.
[09:46] Lina: We'll prepare a trimmed index and metadata fields.
[09:50] Tom: About quotas/rate limits on hosted? we might burst more than expected.
[09:55] Priya: Hosted supports burst capacity and you can buy reserved throughput for predictable peaks. For the pilot we can raise limits.
[10:05] Aisha: Do you have any concerns if we run the hosted pilot with anonymized production-like data?
[10:11] Jordan: No concerns as long as data is anonymized; we'll still recommend KMS and a short retention for that project.
[10:18] (screen share ends)
[10:22] (discussion of integration specifics, API keys, and secret rotation)
[11:05] Priya: Ok wrapping up the demo, we'll share a replay link and the code snippets.
[11:12] Jordan: Recap of next steps: send pricing and pilot options, SE to run 48-hour bench, customer to share sample queries and index schema, schedule deep-dive with platform team.
[11:25] Aisha: thanks everyone, this was helpful — appreciate the concrete numbers.
[11:30] Tom: Thanks, we'll aim to get artifacts to you by end of week.
[11:34] Jordan: Great, we'll follow up in email.

(Recording notes: occasional minor ASR errors — e.g., "rerank" transcribed as "re-rank" or "red wood" for Redwood in a couple spots.)
